feedback: Written before this candidate races. The evidence comes from iterations 0 and 1. Iteration 0 (±0.04 m row, 12 mm footprints) lost the line about once per run, and every run went off track at max_error about 0.063 m. Iteration 1 (±0.06 m, 16 mm footprints, 0.6 kg, y = 0.03 m) removed line losses to zero on all tracks, but every run still went off track, with max_error at 0.0610 to 0.0613 m on all three tracks and progress of 0.10 to 0.21. Because the error is nearly identical across tracks, I read it as a steady drift, perhaps from the motor mismatch, rather than a sensing problem. For that reason I have moved the row to y = 0.05 m as you proposed, and I have raised ki to remove the bias, keeping kp and kd fixed. Body width cannot relax the 0.06 m off-track limit, so geometry only matters through sensing and lead. The next race will decide the direction. If line_loss_events stays at zero and max_error drops below 0.06 m, keep the geometry as it is and do not change the span. If line losses return on the slalom or s-bend, the span is too narrow for the tape at the offsets reached, so widen it. If max_error stays at about 0.061 m with zero line losses, the controller bias is not being removed, and geometry is not the lever.
requested_changes: If the next race shows line_loss_events of 1 or more on the slalom or s-bend, widen the sensor span to x = -0.08, -0.0533, -0.0267, 0, 0.0267, 0.0533, 0.08 (seven sensors, y = 0.05), since iteration 0 lost the tape near ±0.05 m and every run went off track.

If line losses are zero but max_error stays above 0.06 m on the oval and the forward row is not reducing it, try a narrower sensor footprint (sensor_size 0.012) with the same positions, because iteration 0 with 12 mm sensors gave a cleaner graded signal, and steering_oscillation in iteration 1 (0.137 to 0.165) was driven by the 16 mm footprint.
If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 with the forward row at y = 0.05 m, reduce mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg to cut yaw inertia so the body can correct faster, keeping the sensor geometry fixed.
